question: Is SCF v7.0 predatory because only 10 percent is upfront, and can SDF block my app from mainnet or take it down?

golden.answer:
A grounded answer consults the live Stellar Scout directory or research data, directly answers the question with source-supported content, and dates any version-, provider-, or availability-sensitive claim. As of 2026-11-02, the verified sources supported this observed answer:

SCF payment terms and Stellar Mainnet authority are separate. As of **2026-11-02**, the published Build Award schedule is **10% on award acceptance, 20% after MVP, 30% after Testnet/equivalent, and 40% after verified Mainnet launch plus UX readiness**; for Integration Track awards, the final 40% instead releases when the project meets its committed, panel-ratified onchain metric, not on Mainnet launch alone. Later payments require verified deliverables. Current public guidelines require each completion form within 90 calendar days of the preceding payment and allow SDF, absent timely written delay notice and acknowledgement, to deem unpaid tranches forfeited and the award terminated. If a participant breaches the Official Rules' use-of-funds terms (Sections 3 and 3A) or the Program Policies, SDF may, at its sole discretion, rescind the award or require repayment of disbursed funds; that is not automatic clawback. Project-specific agreements and future terms may differ.

That structure shifts execution and cash-flow risk to recipients; whether it is 'predatory' or fair is an evaluative judgment, not established by the 10% fact alone. SDF can administer, suspend, modify, or end its grants and control its sites/branding. That does **not** create a unilateral protocol switch to delete an independently operated Mainnet contract/app, though an app can depend on its own admins, issuers, front end, SDF-operated services, and network/quorum choices.

The dated example is illustrative: a later grounded answer should report what the same source basis supports at its own observation time while preserving the stable distinctions above.
keyFacts: Presents specific source-supported content as a current or dated observation.
Makes the as-of date visible for every changeable roster, status, version, or measurement.
Treats grant administration and protocol erasure of an independently run app as different.
avoid: Do NOT infer fairness/predation from 10% alone, claim already-paid funds are automatically clawed back, or duplicate the current-round/deadline answer here.
Do NOT claim SCF acceptance gives SDF unilateral protocol power to delete a Mainnet app.
Do NOT present version-, provider-, interface-, or availability-sensitive observations as timeless; date the changeable part without weakening stable protocol or historical facts.
Do NOT use an unsupported memory claim as a current SCF v7 fact.
